d9e82f79cc: Running a Full Node: Genoryn Krypton on Linux, Windows and macOS
54ac53e20e: A full node is a program that downloads every block and checks every one of them against every rule. It is how you use Genoryn Krypton without trusting anybody, and how the network stays in the hands of the people who use it. This guide takes you from nothing to a running node on Linux, Windows or macOS.
459cae668f: A full node is the program <0/>. It connects to other nodes, downloads the whole blockchain from the first block, and <1>validates</1> it: the proof of work of every block, the zero-knowledge proof of every transfer, that no coin is spent twice, that no block pays out more than the rules allow. After that it keeps up, one block a minute, and passes what it has checked on to others.
2147b7376c: The wallet does not need one. Its <0>light mode</0> verifies the proof of work behind what nodes tell it and is a sound choice for everyday use. A full node goes further: it checks everything, and asks nobody.
32455ca530: Why a full node is worth running
e585d124eb: Your node has verified every GNR you are paid, back to the block that created it. A block that breaks a rule does not exist for it, however much mining power stands behind it.
a4a9a0f91a: A wallet on your own node asks no other computer about your payments. Nothing about what you hold or whom you pay leaves the house.
6f06d9e5a5: Your node relays blocks and transactions and serves nodes that are catching up. More honest nodes make the network harder to split or censor.
279db5fb44: The rules of Genoryn Krypton are whatever the nodes of the people who accept it enforce. Running one is how you have a say, and the only way.
5f1cb20625: Your miner depends on no one
ebb841d1ac: A miner gets its work from a node. With your own, no outage or decision of someone else's node can stop it.
3fe6ed1e48: Build on it: an explorer, a shop, a payment checker. The API answers on your computer, with no limits and no one in between.
da5ba92679: Running a node is safe and cheap, but not free of things to know.
4fe9daeeac: <0>Keep your wallet safe as always.</0> A node holds no keys and no coins. Your wallet does: write the 24 words on paper, and never type them into a website or give them to a person.
b416efcb24: <0>Bandwidth.</0> Day to day a node moves one small block a minute. If it accepts incoming connections, it also sends the chain to nodes that are syncing. On a metered connection, keep it outbound-only or lower its peer limits (<1>tuning</1>).
e2008bc0cb: <0>Disk.</0> about 0.5 GB at block 21,800, growing with use. A node cannot discard old blocks yet.
5fb0250cc6: <0>The first sync takes a while</0> and keeps the processor busy: every proof since the first block is verified. On a fast desktop processor (Intel Core Ultra 9 285K) it took 32 minutes at block 21,800, on 19 November 2026; a slower computer needs longer, and the time grows with the chain.
055661405e: <0>Antivirus.</0> Some programs distrust anything that talks to many computers or uses a graphics card. Verify your download instead of switching protection off.
5fa0a4b71f: <0>The law.</0> Cryptocurrencies are restricted in some countries. Find out what applies where you live.
898f0906f7: <0>Being a target.</0> A listening node is a computer on the internet, like a web server. The node is written to give peers nothing to hold on to (<1>how</1>), and the wallet's own node accepts no incoming connections unless you say so.
